'''Kevin Dallas Martin Jr.''' (born February 1, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for [[Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball|Western Carolina University]], where in his junior year, he averaged 24.9 points per game, which ranked second in the nation. After three years at Western Carolina, he entered the [[2004 NBA draft]] and was selected with the 26th overall pick by the [[Sacramento Kings]].

==Early life==
Martin was born in [[Zanesville, Ohio]], to Kevin Sr. and Marilyn Martin. He grew up idolizing [[Michael Jordan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kmart23.com/about-youth.html|title=Kevin Martin Official Site - Youth|work=KMart23.com|publisher=Kevin Martin Official|access-date=October 16, 2013}}</ref> He played for [[Zanesville High School]] and was fourth in the voting for [[Ohio Mr. Basketball]] as a [[Senior (education)|Senior]], finishing behind the first [[Tenth grade#United States|Sophomore]] winner [[LeBron James]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jenni|last=Carlson|url=http://newsok.com/thunders-kevin-martin-remains-a-hometown-hero/article/3746197|title=Thunder's Kevin Martin remains a hometown hero|work=NewsOk.com|date=January 15, 2013|access-date=January 16, 2013}}</ref>

==College career==
He received a full scholarship to [[Western Carolina University]], where he majored in sport management. On November 22, 2002, Martin scored a college career-high 46 points in a loss against [[Coastal Carolina Chanticleers men's basketball|Coastal Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112202aaa.html|title=WCU Men's Basketball Falls to Coastal Carolina, 77-72, in Season Opener|work=CatamountSports.com|date=November 22, 2002|access-date=August 31, 2005|archive-date=March 8, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308134512/http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112202aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 21, 2003, Martin scored 44 points in a loss against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112203aaa.html|title=Georgia Holds on for 78-67 Win over Western Carolina|work=CatamountSports.com|date=November 21, 2003|access-date=August 31, 2005|archive-date=October 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022143109/http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/112203aaa.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He ranks fourth all-time on Western Carolina's scoring list with 1,838 points. Martin averaged 23.3 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.7 assists per game during his three years in college.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kevin-martin-1.html|title=Kevin Martin stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=March 19, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Sacramento Kings (2004–2010)===
Martin was a standout while at Western Carolina. Due to his success, he was selected by the Sacramento Kings with the 26th overall pick in the [[2004 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062404aaa.html|title=WCU's Kevin Martin Goes in First Round to Sacramento Kings in NBA Draft|work=CatamountSports.com|date=June 24, 2004|access-date=August 31, 2005|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923200839/http://www.catamountsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062404aaa.html|archive-date=September 23, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[File:kevinmartin.jpg|thumb|left|Martin in 2005 during his tenure with the Kings]]

In the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]], Martin averaged 2.9 points, 1.3 rebounds and 0.5 assists per game, and played sparingly, averaging just 10 minutes a game.

Martin showed much improvement the following year, averaging 10.8 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Martin also started from time to time during the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]] in part by the injury of [[Bonzi Wells]]. This included a start at [[small forward]] due to [[Metta World Peace|Ron Artest]] being suspended for Game Two of the team's first-round playoff series against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] following a flagrant foul (elbow to the head) on [[Manu Ginóbili]]. He is best known in that series for making the game winning buzzer beater in Game 3 in Sacramento that gave the Kings a 1–2 series against the Spurs. His shot was also over the [[San Antonio Spurs]]' [[Tim Duncan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=260428023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306185205/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=260428023|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2016|title=Kings return the favor, beat Spurs at the buzzer|work=ESPN.com|date=April 29, 2006|access-date=April 29, 2006}}</ref>

When interviewed on a segment by [[NBA on TNT|TNT]] during a game, Martin credited [[Doug Christie (basketball)|Doug Christie]] for helping him learn how to defend in the NBA. Likewise, Martin also credited [[Cuttino Mobley]] for helping him with his shooting. Martin played behind both guards during their tenure with the Kings.

In the general managers' survey at the start of the 2006–07 NBA season, Martin tied for second as the player most likely to have a breakout campaign, behind the [[Orlando Magic]]'s [[Dwight Howard]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/preview2006/gmsurvey_players.html|title=GM Survey: Best Players|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 5, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070630075055/http://www.nba.com/preview2006/gmsurvey_players.html|archive-date=June 30, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the 2006–07 season, Martin proved himself to be among the top scorers in the NBA, averaging 20.2 points per game, while averaging 4.3 rebounds and 2.2 assists, all career highs. He is also one of the best shooters in the league with a 47.3% shooting percentage from the field and 38.1% from beyond the three-point arc (along with 84.4% FT shooting). Martin finished second to [[Monta Ellis]] in the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]]. Ellis edged Martin by three points in the closest voting in the award's history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2850222|title=Ellis edges Martin, wins most improved award|work=ESPN.com|date=April 26, 2007|access-date=April 26, 2007}}</ref>

On March 17, 2007, Martin led the Kings to a 95–83 road win over the Orlando Magic and joined [[Nate Archibald]] as the only other player in NBA history to score at least 20 points in a game with only one field goal made. Martin tallied 20 points on 1-8 FG from the field (1–1 3pt) while knocking down 17-20 FT from the foul line.

On August 28, 2007, the [[Sacramento Kings]] and Martin agreed to a 5-year, $55 million deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/kings-reward-kevin-martin-with-extension-1.635154|title=Kings reward Kevin Martin with extension|work=CBC.ca|date=August 28, 2007|access-date=August 28, 2007}}</ref>
[[File:Kevin Martin Sacramento Kings 2008-02-13 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|Martin with the Kings in 2008]]
Martin got off to a fast start to the NBA season, while in the first 15 games was the NBA's leading scorer with 29.6 PPG. Martin finished the season 6th in the NBA in scoring at 23.7 [[Points per game|PPG]], 4.5 [[Rebound (basketball)|RPG]], 2.1 [[Assists per game|APG]] and averaging 45% from the court and 40% from three-point range.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player?season=2008&seasontype=2|title=NBA Player Scoring Per Game Statistics - 2007-08|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 19, 2008}}</ref> However, he missed 17 games due to a groin injury. Also during the year, on March 7, 2008, Martin scored 48 points in a loss against the Minnesota Timberwolves.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280307023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107124002/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280307023|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 7, 2009|title=Martin's career-high 48 points not enough to topple Timberwolves|work=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2008|access-date=March 8, 2008}}</ref>

Martin became the leader of the team following the [[Ron Artest]] trade during the offseason. He started the season strong, however he suffered an ankle injury which kept him out 15 games. He returned, but re-aggravated his injury shortly thereafter. After returning again, he helped the Kings snap a 6-game losing streak. Martin averaged 24.6 points per game during the remainder of the season, including an overtime loss on April 1, 2009, against the [[Golden State Warriors]], in which he scored a career-high 50 points and became the first King to score 50-plus since [[Chris Webber]] in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290401009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090404114824/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=290401009|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 4, 2009|title=Ellis, Warriors survive Martin, Kings in overtime|work=ESPN.com|date=April 2, 2009|access-date=April 2, 2009}}</ref> On November 2, 2009, Martin scored 48 points including 7–10 from three-point range to lead the Kings to an overtime victory over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291102023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091109045115/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291102023|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 9, 2009|title=Martin scores 48 as Kings beat Grizzlies in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2009|access-date=November 3, 2009}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2010–2012)===
Martin was traded during the 2009–10 season to the [[Houston Rockets]] on February 18, 2010, as part of a three-way trade including the [[New York Knicks]] and the [[Sacramento Kings]], sending [[Larry Hughes]], [[Joey Dorsey]], and [[Carl Landry]] to Sacramento.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4924836|title=T-Mac traded in 3-team deal|work=ESPN.com|date=February 19, 2010|access-date=February 19, 2010}}</ref> In his debut as a Rocket, Martin scored just 3–16 from the field, but 8–9 from the line, ending the game with 14 points, in a 125–115 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20100220/INDHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Ford, Pacers spoil Martin's debut in Houston|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2010|access-date=March 19, 2016}}</ref> On April 12, in his first game back in Sacramento's Arco Arena, Martin scored 39 points, scoring 11 of 20, making all 16 of his foul shot attempts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=300412023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110404071039/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=300412023|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 4, 2011|title=Martin helps Rockets triumph in his return to Sacramento|work=ESPN.com|date=April 13, 2010|access-date=April 13, 2010}}</ref>

On December 11, 2010, Martin scored 40 points in a 110–95 win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=301211010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160329081454/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=301211010|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 29, 2016|title=Rockets come up short as Blazers overcome Kevin Martin's 45 points|work=ESPN.com|date=December 12, 2010|access-date=December 12, 2010}}</ref> and went on to score a season-high 45 points in a loss against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on January 5, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=310105010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305094749/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?id=310105010|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 5, 2016|title=Rockets come up short as Blazers overcome Kevin Martin's 45 points|work=ESPN.com|date=January 6, 2011|access-date=January 6, 2011}}</ref> By the end of the season he averaged 23.5 points per game in 32 minutes per game. Martin shot .383 at the three-point line, and he was also near .900 from free throw range. Martin averaged 7.4 made free throws per game, second in the NBA to only [[Kevin Durant]].

After commissioner [[David Stern]], acting as owner of the [[New Orleans Hornets]] at the time, vetoed a three-team deal involving the Rockets and the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] that would have sent Martin, [[Luis Scola]], [[Goran Dragić]], and [[Lamar Odom]] to New Orleans, he stayed with Houston for the lockout-shortened season. Martin suffered a shoulder injury on February 2. He tried to play through the injury but ended up re-aggravating the injury when he ran into a screen against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] on March 11. An MRI revealed a labral tear in his right shoulder, and he missed the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen|url=http://blog.chron.com/ultimaterockets/2012/03/cause-for-martins-injury-discovered/|title=Cause for Martin's injury discovered|work=Chron.com|date=March 22, 2012|access-date=March 22, 2012}}</ref> With new rules regarding foul calls, in addition to playing injured, Martin's numbers dropped, averaging just 17.1 points per game, the worst in his career as a full-time starter. While he was still able to make a high percentage of his free throws, he only got to the line about half as often as the previous season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/2394/kevin-martin|title=Kevin Martin stats|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 7, 2012}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2012–2013)===
On October 27, 2012, Martin was traded along with [[Jeremy Lamb]] and three future draft picks to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for [[James Harden]], [[Daequan Cook]], [[Lazar Hayward]], and [[Cole Aldrich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/27/james-harden-traded-to-rockets.ap/|title=Thunder trade Harden to Rockets for Martin, Lamb and picks|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2012|access-date=October 27, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031022030/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/27/james-harden-traded-to-rockets.ap/|archive-date=October 31, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In game six of the Western Conference Quarterfinals, Martin scored 25 points in a 103–94 win, as the Thunder eliminated his former team the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400459784|title=Kevin Durant, Thunder eliminate Rockets in 6 games|work=ESPN.com|date=May 4, 2013|access-date=May 4, 2013}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2013–2016)===
On July 2, 2013, it was reported Martin had agreed to sign a four-year, $28 million contract with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/nba--kevin-martin-to-sign-with-timberwolves-000243254.html|title=Kevin Martin to sign with Timberwolves|work=Yahoo.com|date=July 2, 2013|access-date=July 2, 2013}}</ref> Martin reportedly also received interest from the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. On July 11, 2013, he was officially acquired by the Timberwolves as part of a three-team trade involving the Thunder and the Bucks that sent the rights to [[Szymon Szewczyk]] to Oklahoma City and [[Luke Ridnour]] to Milwaukee. <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-acquire-veteran-guard-kevin-martin|title=Wolves Acquire Veteran Guard Kevin Martin|work=NBA.com|date=July 11, 2013|access-date=July 11, 2013}}</ref> On November 3, 2013, Martin scored 30 points, including 5–5 three-pointers as the Timberwolves defeated the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Jerry|last=Zgoda|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/230425061.html|title=Wolves defeat Knicks, go to 3-0|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=November 4, 2013|access-date=November 4, 2013|archive-date=November 7, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131107023946/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/230425061.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 25, 2014, Martin was sidelined for six to eight weeks after undergoing surgery to repair a fracture in his right wrist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/kevin-martin-injury-update-0|title=Kevin Martin Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=November 25, 2014|access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref>

On March 1, 2016, Martin was waived by the Timberwolves in a buyout agreement.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-waive-guard-kevin-martin|title=Timberwolves Waive Guard Kevin Martin|work=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2016|access-date=March 9, 2016}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2016)===
On March 9, 2016, Martin signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-kevin-martin|title=SPURS SIGN KEVIN MARTIN|work=NBA.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=March 9, 2016}}</ref> His best effort as a Spur came on April 8, 2016, when he scored 17 points against the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/martike02/gamelog/2016/|title=Kevin Martin 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 26, 2016}}</ref> Martin's final appearance came on May 12, 2016, in the Spurs' loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in Game 6 of the Western Conference semi-finals; he recorded two rebounds in just under six minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160512/SASOKC/gameinfo.html |title=Thunder beat Spurs, advance to Western Conference finals |work=NBA.com |date=May 12, 2016 |access-date=April 15, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160516123348/http://www.nba.com/games/20160512/SASOKC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=May 16, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Retirement===
On November 24, 2016, Martin announced his retirement from the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zanesvilletimesrecorder.com/story/sports/local/2016/11/25/kevin-martin-announces-retirement-ad/94426040/|title=Kevin Martin announces retirement in ad|work=zanesvilletimesrecorder.com|date=November 25, 2016|access-date=November 26, 2016}}</ref>

==Player profile==
[[File:20140101 Kevin Martin (8).JPG|thumb|Martin attacking the rim during a game in 2014]]
Standing at six feet, seven inches tall and weighing in at 200 pounds, Martin played the [[shooting guard]] position. With a career points-per-game average of 17.4, he established himself as one of the most efficient scorers in the NBA. Despite his unorthodox shooting stroke and skinny frame, he made significant contributions offensively. He was also known for his quickness. Martin went to the free throw line frequently and shot a great percentage; he led the NBA in free throws made in [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11]]. He was considered an average defender who had good awareness but lacked strength.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player?season=2011|title=NBA Player Free-Throw Shooting Statistics - 2010-11|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 17, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Kevin-Martin-3450/|title= DraftExpressProfile: Kevin Martin, Stats, Comparisons, and Outlook |work=DraftExpress.com|access-date=August 3, 2013}}</ref> In a 2010 interview, [[Reggie Miller]] was asked which NBA players reminded him of his own playing style. Miller responded: "Game-wise I would say [[Richard Hamilton (basketball)|Richard Hamilton]] and Kevin Martin. Thin, great coming off screens, can knock down [[Three-point field goal|threes]]."<ref>{{cite news|first=Fred|last=Bierman|url=http://offthedribble.blogs.nytimes.com/2010/01/29/q-a-with-reggie-miller/?_r=0|title=Q. & A. With Reggie Miller|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=January 29, 2010|access-date=January 29, 2010}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==
On October 1, 2019, the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) announced their new ownership group, which included Martin.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bullets announce new ownership group, including former NBA player Kevin Martin|url=https://www.brisbanebullets.com.au/news/article/bullets-announce-new-ownership-group-including-former-nba-player-kevin-martin|date=October 1, 2019|website=brisbanebullets.com.au|access-date=October 2, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2007, Martin traveled to [[Johannesburg, South Africa]] to participate in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] Program and Habitat for Humanity.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kmart23.com/giving-back-int.html|title=Kevin Martin Official Site-Community Giving-International|work=KMart23.com|publisher=Kevin Martin Official|access-date=August 13, 2011|archive-date=December 16, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121216180356/http://www.kmart23.com/giving-back-int.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In June 2010, Martin volunteered to donate money to pay for the funeral of Kasey King-Thomas, a six-year-old boy who died in a school bus accident near Martin's hometown. Martin also voiced his support for an Ohio law requiring [[seat belts in school buses]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Kathy |last=Thompson |url=http://www.zanesvilletimesrecorder.com/article/20100604/UPDATES01/100604025/NBA-star-pays-for-child-s-funeral |title=NBA star pays for child's funeral |work=Zanesville Times Recorder |date=June 4, 2010 |access-date=June 12, 2010 |archive-date=February 17, 2013 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217024305/http://www.zanesvilletimesrecorder.com/article/20100604/UPDATES01/100604025/NBA-star-pays-for-child-s-funeral |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Martin married Jill Arnold on July 15, 2011, in [[Clearwater Beach, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://graceormonde.com/uncategorized/tampa-wedding-videographers/|title=ALMOST A DECADE: JILL & KEVIN GET MARRIED|work=GraceOrmonde.com|date=July 15, 2011|access-date=July 24, 2011}}</ref>
